definitions.explanation: A pointed length of wood, metal, or concrete driven into the ground as a support, marker, or foundation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{土地|とち}→土地：02226_tochi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{境界|きょうかい}→境界：12096_kyoukai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{杭|くい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{立|た}てた→立てる：01196_tateru⟧。
examples.english: I put up stakes at the land boundary.

examples.japanese: ⟦{建物|たてもの}→建物：01458_tatemono⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{基礎|きそ}→基礎：03981_kiso⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧、⟦{深|ふか}く→深い：01211_fukai⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧{杭|くい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{打|う}ち{込|こ}んだ→打ち込む：04229_uchikomu⟧。
examples.english: We drove piles deep down as the foundation for the building.

notes:
Used both for small ground stakes (tent pegs, boundary markers) and for large engineering piles used as building foundations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {杭|くい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧: to drive a stake
- {杭|くい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{打|う}ち{込|こ}む→打ち込む：04229_uchikomu⟧: to drive a stake/pile in (deeper, more forceful)
- {杭|くい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{立|た}てる→立てる：01196_tateru⟧: to stand a stake up
- ⟦{基礎|きそ}→基礎：03981_kiso⟧{杭|くい}: foundation pile

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
でる{杭|くい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{打|う}たれる→打つ：01221_utsu⟧: 'the stake that sticks out gets hammered down' — a well-known proverb meaning that people who stand out tend to be criticized or held back.
